root_idea.summary: The root centers on covering or filling one thing with another until it is level with it, and extends to overwhelming, rising over, or predominating.
root_idea.development: From covering and leveling a well or other object, the lexicon develops usages for the sea, abundant or overpowering events, and the supreme overwhelming event; hair-cutting is related through leveling, while mounting and rising are reported extensions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Standalone Quran-attested nominal headword, normalized to the classical citation form طَامَّةٌ.

senses.definition: An overwhelming calamity or event, one that surpasses and overcomes others.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine noun derived from the sense of prevailing or overtaking; the Quranic occurrence is the definite expression الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَى.

senses.definition: The Resurrection, the supreme overwhelming event.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-specific designation in الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَى; it is so called because it surpasses and predominates over everything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water or a torrent: to become abundant, rise high, and predominate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water, a valley torrent, or a watercourse; the associated result may be that the torrent overwhelms its channel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill, choke, or cover something so that it becomes level with the surrounding ground; to fill a vessel to overflowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of filling a well or other hollow with earth or dust, covering an object with earth, or filling a vessel until its contents overflow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an affair, event, sedition, or calamity: to rise to prominence, prevail, become vehement, or become formidable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of rising and predominating; it may describe an evil exceeding its ordinary limit or an event that overcomes others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mount or leap upon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a stallion mounting a mare and of a bird alighting or mounting on the top of a tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move swiftly or run easily; to go forth across the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a man or horse and of easy, rapid running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trim or cut hair, including cutting it off entirely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively with the hair or head; the amount removed may range from part of the hair to all of it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plait or twist hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct hair-grooming usage from cutting or trimming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alight upon a branch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II usage applied to a bird.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of hair: to reach or approach the time when it should be cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV expression describes hair as having grown to the point of needing cutting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a rivulet, well, or similar depression: to become filled with earth or dust until level with the surrounding ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VII intransitive resultative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To swim in the midst of the sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reduplicated Form I usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sea: to become full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate reported application of the reduplicated form to the sea itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have an impediment or barbarousness in speech, so that one does not speak clearly or correctly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A speech-related usage of the reduplicated form; the statement concerns defective or indistinct utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is explained as referring to the sea because it overwhelms what is in it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water, especially abundant water; also the rubbish, scum, or similar material floating on or driven along by water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The water and surface-debris applications are reported as related uses of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large number or multitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal extension illustrated in the expression الطِّمِّ وَالرِّمِّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wonderful or extraordinary thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported nominal meaning, synonymous with something astonishing or remarkable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A male ostrich.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is associated in the source with the bird’s lightness of pace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A courser or swift horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is associated either with quick, easy running or metaphorically with the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large male.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported nominal use explained through the description of the head as bare or trimmed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possibly a clever or capable person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported in one lexicographical reading but is disputed as a likely transcription error for طَمٌّ, the filling or compressing sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or congregated body of people, especially its midst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a gathered group and for the central part of that group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Error, deviation from the right course, confusion, or perplexity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes being unable to see or follow the right course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dirt or filth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun meaning what is dirty or impure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Human dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used idiomatically in an expression for wallowing in one’s own dung.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion of herbage, mostly dry or dried-up herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a quantity or patch of such vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hardy, strong, or sturdy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied in the cited usage to a mature or well-developed beast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive adjectival description of a horse’s speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medley or multitude of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for a mixed or numerous body of people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry, especially a vehement cry that overcomes everything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic specialization of the noun, distinct from its Quranic designation of the Resurrection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose speech is indistinct, incorrect, or impeded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a speaker characterized by barbarousness or lack of clear articulation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foreigners or non-Arabic-speaking people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported plural application associated with طِمْطِمٌ; it occurs in an explanation of a poetic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of sheep with small ears and fleshy folds resembling an ox’s dewlaps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional animal term associated with Yemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impediment or barbarousness in speech that makes it unclear or incorrect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun of the speech-related reduplicated form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle or central part of the sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal derivative referring to the sea’s midst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main part or midst of a fire; much fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the central or abundant mass, reported in a traditional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More vehement or severe annoyance, molestation, harm, or hurt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective used in a comparative or emphatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Legs of a beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A meaning reported in one lexicographical account and disputed by another account that understands the word as a speed adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Brisk, active, or quick in pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the word in a description of a she-camel or quick-moving beast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Plaited or twisted hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of hair that has been arranged in this way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A head whose hair has been cut off entirely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of a closely shaven or completely cut head.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers rising or predominating water, filling or covering, and the proverb’s prevailing-event extension.
Affair, event, sedition, or calamity becoming formidable or prevailing.
Mounting a mare or alighting on a tree.
Swift or easy running and going across the earth.
Cutting hair and plaiting or twisting it.
Hair approaching the time for cutting.
A watercourse or well becoming filled and level.
Water and floating or driven rubbish and scum.
Disputed report of a clever or capable person.
Human dung and its idiomatic use.
Calamity that predominates, or a great and formidable thing.
The Resurrection as the supreme overwhelming event.
Indistinct speech and the reported plural use for foreigners; the poetic thunder interpretation is contextual rather than a separate headword sense.
Much fire or the main part of fire.
Intensive adjective for severe harm or annoyance.
Disputed alternatives: legs of a beast, or brisk and quick in pace.
A head whose hair is completely cut off.

cautions: The canonical QAC root طمم is matched to the contracted Lane and Maqāyīs heading طم; this is a root-matching convention, not a claim that the roots are unrelated.
